## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Samathavāra* ("How each offense is settled") constitutes a chapter within the *Parivāra*, the concluding analytic treatise of the Pali *Vinaya Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. The text systematically maps the Vinaya offenses and rules to the seven traditional legal procedures (*samatha* or *adhikaraṇasamatha*) employed for the settlement of monastic disputes and legal issues [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations of the text include an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Textual reuse analyses recorded by DharmaNexus identify 151 matching passages shared across 25 other Pali texts, demonstrating dense internal cross-referencing within the *Vinaya Piṭaka* [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive textual overlaps are with other analytical sections of the *Parivāra*, specifically the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4), *Samathabheda* (Pvr 5), *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 1.1), other homonymous *Samathavāra* chapters (such as Pvr 2.7, Pvr 2.15, and Pvr 1.15), and the *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11), alongside citations in the *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus reports any cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].

None of the surveyed reference passages discuss this specific chapter of the *Parivāra*; they instead concern the meditative cultivation of serenity (*samatha*), the *Samathakkhandhaka* of the *Cullavagga*, the author Śamathadeva, or *adhikaraṇa-śamatha* in general non-canonical contexts.
